text:
I cry out to your livid belly of wind,

to the narrow heart of your roosters,

to their red whips, to the rays

that riddle your hollow firmament.


I seek the edge of unfolding,

to steal myself as fruit from my normal stems,

to free myself in your acid horses

and to anoint your towers with my advent.


If you came with me to the undulating

high hill of being, where living blood

turns into the symbol of ice...


But who will be able to stop the dawn,

already lifting the shell of its route,

its raptors of light over your flight.




1951

translation.title: I Cry Out to Your Livid Belly of Wind...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Barral's turbulent apostrophe and the dawn's raptors of light.
